posts.text:
Europe in 1618: a patchwork of empires and hundreds of small states, about to tip into 30 years of war. The map before the storm.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The spark came in May 1618, when Bohemian Protestant nobles threw Catholic imperial officials out of a window at Prague Castle. History calls it the Defenestration of Prague.

2/ The dark patch in the middle is the Holy Roman Empire, a loose patchwork of states under the emperor. The Habsburgs, in yellow, held Austria and the Bohemian lands at its core. The mapmaker notes not every state is shown.
3/ The war spread. In 1630 Sweden entered as a Lutheran power and won major victories under Gustavus Adolphus.
4/ Plot twist: Catholic France joined in 1635 on the side of Protestant Sweden and the Dutch. Its aim was to weaken the Habsburgs, who ruled both Austria and Spain.
5/ The Peace of Westphalia ended it on 24 October 1648. Sweden gained Swedish Pomerania, Bremen and Verden, and France gained territory in Alsace and Lorraine.
6/ The toll: modern estimates run from 4.5 to 8 million dead, mostly civilians. Some German regions reported population drops of over half, though that includes people who fled.
Was this a religious war or a power struggle in disguise? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
